Priya (rt): ran an nsys capture against the prod-replay with seq_len=2048 and hit repeated long stalls that line up with kernel compile events. command I used: `nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda --output=out.nsys-rep --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi:start,end -- ./run_inference --model rwd-7b --seq 2048`. KV cache counters spike at the same timestamps. anyone seen this pattern before?

JJ: can you paste the kernel names from the timeline? are these `triton_jit_compile` or XLA compiles? :eyes:

Priya (rt): timeline snippet shows repeated `triton_jit_compile` entries followed by `attention_forward` launches. nvlink transfers spike right after. attached a small `nsys` extract I pulled: `nsys stats out.nsys-rep | grep -i compile` (triton_jit_compile x 14, total compile time ~850ms).

Sam T: hypothesis — compile is triggered when selector picks a different codepath after seeing a new seq/batch shape. dynamic batching mixing seq=512 and 2048 could be creating many unique cache keys, causing JIT churn. did you check batch padding distribution?

Elena M: I ran a quick nvprof on a local repro and saw repeated `triton::compile` calls where the kernel name hash changes each time. looks like cache key includes exact seq and batch dims rather than normalized buckets. tiny snippet of what I found in logs: `kernel_key = f"{arch}:{seq}:{batch}:{att_cfg}"` -> that will explode combinatorially.

Priya (rt): confirmed — cache keys include `max_seq` field. when we mix 512/2048, the runtime compiles both variants. KV cache eviction timestamps line up since compiled kernels allocate GPU memory and push out cached KV entries.

JJ: easy test: try forcing a canonical path by setting `INFER_CANONICALIZE_SEQ=1` or force-disable compile with `TRITON_DISABLE_COMPILE=1` and see latency impact.

Sam T: try this repro trace command to collect focused compile metrics: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none --output=diag.nsys -- ./repro --batch-schedule 'mix:512,2048'` then `nsys stats diag.nsys | grep -i compile`. also capture `nvprof --print-gpu-trace` for kernel names.

Priya (rt): running the repro now on canary, will post numbers in ~20m. attaching small perfetto link for context: https://perf.redwood/reports/1955 (private).

deploy-bot: build 0.23.7 deployed to canary.

Elena M: quick local hack — normalizing seq to nearest power-of-two before keying cut my compile events by ~70% in a lightweight test. padding to 2048 for mixed requests collapsed variants.

JJ: nice find. long-term, selector should normalize shapes before generating kernel cache keys. filed an issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/2345 (prototype plan inside).

Sam T: additional mitigation: increase kernel-cache size and make it per-device (not per-worker process) so separate worker processes don't evict each other's compiled kernels. also add a small TTL for compiled kernels that are rarely used.

Priya (rt): experiment finished. numbers: baseline median p99 latency 210ms, after padding canonicalization median p99 155ms. compile-time contribution dropped from ~45ms per-request to ~5ms. compile_count: 12 -> 2 during the run.

Elena M: :tada: great improvement. next steps: (1) selector normalization PR, (2) kernel-cache policy tweak (per-device + TTL), (3) add nsys smoke test in CI that asserts compile events < threshold for mixed-batch replay.

JJ: I'll take the selector normalization PR. Sam, can you own cache policy changes and the per-device cache design? Priya — can you wire up the nsys smoke-test + repro harness and link it to the perf dashboard?

Priya (rt): yep, will open PRs and a reproducible test. thanks all :raised_hands:

Sam T: quick note for the runbook — if you see compile spikes, set `TRITON_COMPILE_DEBUG=1` and capture `nsys` with `--sample=none` to avoid sampling noise, then grep `triton_jit_compile` and check kernel key variance.

JJ: added a short task in the sprint backlog under infra/perf.

Elena M: also let's add a small logging field in the runtime that prints normalized key components when debug is enabled, that will speed triage.

Priya (rt): putting links and artifacts in the issue. closing this thread for now, will ping when PRs land.
